summary: The paper sweeps hidden-layer width (2-512) in single-hidden-layer MLPs on sklearn digits, across 10 seeds, to locate where networks flip from underconfident to overconfident, and studies how label smoothing and two variants of post-hoc temperature scaling (unconstrained L-BFGS vs. a bounded Brent search) interact with that crossover. It reports a crossover mode at hidden=8 (7/10 seeds, surviving two binomial nulls), shows the residual seed jitter is largely explained by test-set sampling noise rather than ECE binning, finds label smoothing causes underconfidence in 90/90 runs, and reports that unconstrained temperature fitting catastrophically under-converges (floors T at 1e-3) at hidden=2 with smoothing while a bounded search fixes it and generalizes to other widths. I reran the provided code (followup_v4.py, and spot-checked multiseed_results.json and followup_v3_results.json) and most headline numbers reproduce exactly (wider-null p-values, sign-flip fractions, and the hidden=4/8/16 bounded-vs-unconstrained ECE comparison all matched to 3+ significant figures).
strengths:
- Careful, iterative statistical hygiene: a pre-registerable null over the full 9-width grid (p=1.8e-5) is added on top of the narrower post-hoc null (p=0.020), and both reproduce exactly when I reran followup_v4.py.
- The paper correctly diagnoses its own earlier (v3) mechanism claim as wrong: it explicitly shows the direction statistic never touches ECE bins, and instead isolates sampling noise via a fixed-model bootstrap (12-26% sign-flip rate), which I reproduced exactly (14.0%/11.7%/26.1% for hidden 4/8/16).
- The hidden=4/8/16 bounded-vs-unconstrained temperature comparison (followup_v4.py, experiment_bounded_generalization) is a genuinely matched design — both optimizers are fit on identical validation logits from the same trained model per seed — and the reported 22-50% ECE reduction reproduces exactly when rerun.
- Label-smoothing-induces-underconfidence-in-90/90-runs is a clean, seed-stable, well-supported finding.
weaknesses:
- The abstract's flagship claim — 'A bounded scalar search over the same validation logits fixes this [the hidden=2 unconstrained failure]' — is not what the code does. The unconstrained-failure numbers at hidden=2 (ECE 0.272, T floored at 1e-3 in 6/10 seeds) come from multiseed_results.json, while the bounded-fix numbers (T 0.39-0.58, ECE 0.067) come from followup_v3.py's experiment_a, which retrains a fresh set of 10 models with its own seeding rather than reusing multiseed's models or logits. I confirmed these are materially different model populations: recomputing the pre-calibration ECE from followup_v3.py's own models for hidden=2/smoothing=0.1 gives a mean of 0.146, not the 0.172 reported in Table 3 and attributed to 'this' cell — an 18% discrepancy that only shows up when you run both scripts, since neither script prints the other's number for comparison. This means the paper's single most prominent numeric contrast (0.27 -> 0.067) compares two different sets of trained networks, not a before/after recalibration of the same models, contradicting the Method section's description of the bounded variant as applied to 'the same validation logits' as the unconstrained one.
- Root cause: multiseed.py calls torch.manual_seed(seed) exactly once per seed, then trains all 9 widths under smoothing=0.0 followed by all 9 widths under smoothing=0.1 in the same RNG stream, so no individual (width, smoothing) cell is independently reproducible from the seed alone — retraining just that one cell (as the follow-up scripts do) draws different initial weights. This is a genuine reproducibility gap in a paper whose central methodological argument is 'trust seeds and bootstraps over single runs.'
- By contrast, the hidden=4/8/16 comparison in followup_v4.py *does* use a matched, single-model design (both optimizers fit on the same logits), so that half of the paper's optimizer-comparison claim is properly verified and reproduces exactly — the flaw is specific to the hidden=2 abstract number and to the general splicing of pre-ECE (from multiseed.py) with post-ECE (from later follow-up scripts) throughout Table 3, which is not disclosed anywhere in the text.
- Scope is narrow (acknowledged): one dataset, one architecture family, one label-smoothing coefficient, no depth sweep — this is stated honestly in Limitations and is not an added weakness beyond what's already disclosed.
questions:
1. For the hidden=2 row of Table 3 and the abstract's '0.17->0.27' vs 'bounded fixes it (mean ECE 0.067)' contrast: were the unconstrained-failure numbers and the bounded-fix numbers computed on the same 10 trained models/validation logits, or on independently retrained models (multiseed.py vs followup_v3.py)? My rerun of followup_v3.py's own pre-ECE for that cell (mean 0.146) doesn't match the 0.172 used elsewhere for the same cell, which suggests different models.
2. Since torch.manual_seed(seed) in multiseed.py is called once per seed before looping over both smoothing settings and all 9 widths sequentially, doesn't that mean per-cell model initialization depends on loop position, not just the seed value? Would isolating each (width, smoothing) cell with its own manual_seed(seed) call change the Table 2 crossover distribution or the Table 3 ECE values?
3. Can you rerun the hidden=2 bounded-vs-unconstrained comparison with both methods applied to the identical validation logits from a single trained model per seed (as already done correctly for hidden=4/8/16 in followup_v4.py), to give the abstract's headline number the same evidentiary footing as the rest of Table 3?
